label: Réduction de 50% du gaspillage alimentaire mondial d'ici 6 ans (ODD 12.3)

sources: IPCC AR6 SYR Figure 4.4 — Food loss and waste reduction identified as ~2 GtCO2eq/yr mitigation potential by 2030
FAO State of Food and Agriculture 2019 — 14% of food lost between harvest and retail; 17% wasted at household and food service level
UNEP Food Waste Index Report 2024 — Household food waste reaches 631 Mt/yr; reducing it could cut 1 GtCO2/yr
IPCC AR6 WGIII Ch.7 — Food demand-side measures including waste reduction offer ~3.7 GtCO2eq/yr combined potential at <$20/tCO2

planetary_limits.note: Lower agricultural land pressure reduces habitat conversion
Food production uses ~70% of global freshwater; waste reduction lowers water footprint
Less food production means less nitrogen fertiliser runoff

societal_indicators.note: If food waste was a country, it would be the 3rd largest GHG emitter; reducing it improves calorie availability

interactions.note: Diet shift reduces food system emissions; waste reduction maximises the value of remaining food production
Smaller agricultural footprint enables land restoration to regenerative practices

methodological_note: Median impact of 2 GtCO2eq/yr calibrated against IPCC AR6 SYR Fig 4.4. High uncertainty (score 3) because food waste reduction involves millions of individual consumer and supply chain actors rather than a discrete policy lever. Pessimistic scenario accounts for structural barriers in global retail (promotions driving over-purchasing), and increasing food waste with income growth in emerging economies. Optimistic scenario assumes digital tracking tools (apps, smart packaging) and cold chain infrastructure deployment in Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia eliminate 58% of post-harvest losses. Projection baseline: SSP2-4.5.
